mcq.q: What is compost manure?
options: Fresh soil from a river bank
A dark crumbly material made when plant and animal wastes rot
mcq.explanation: Compost is organic manure made from rotted wastes.

mcq.q: Why is meat kept out of a compost heap?
options: It makes the compost too dry
It attracts rats and flies and smells bad
mcq.explanation: Meat and fatty food attract pests and create a bad smell.

mcq.q: How wet should a compost heap be?
options: Covered by a pool of water
mcq.explanation: Too dry stops rotting and too wet makes the heap smell sour.

mcq.q: Which sign shows that compost is ready?
options: It is hot and full of whole peelings
It is dark, crumbly and smells like fresh earth
It is wet and smells sour
mcq.explanation: Ready compost looks and smells like soil and the materials cannot be recognised.

mcq.q: Which of these helps to prevent soil erosion?
options: Covering the ground with mulch or grass
mcq.explanation: Covering keeps rain from washing soil away.

mcq.q: What is drip irrigation?
options: Throwing water from a bucket quickly
Letting water fall slowly drop by drop near the roots
Spraying water high into the air
mcq.explanation: Drip irrigation gives small amounts of water directly at the roots.

mcq.q: Why should the holes in a drip pipe be tiny?
mcq.explanation: Small holes give slow drips that soak into the soil.

mcq.q: How far from the plant should the bottle drip be placed?
options: Exactly on top of the stem
mcq.explanation: Close enough for the roots to reach the water.

mcq.q: Which of these is a way of collecting water for the garden?
mcq.explanation: Rainwater tanks store water for dry days.

mcq.q: Which of these crops can be watered with drip irrigation?
mcq.explanation: Drip systems suit row crops such as tomatoes and kale.

mcq.q: Which of these is a fuel used at home for cooking?
mcq.explanation: Charcoal is burnt to give heat.

mcq.q: Why does a lid on a pot save fuel?
options: It keeps the heat in so food cooks faster
It stops the food from cooking
mcq.explanation: Less heat escapes so less fuel is used.

mcq.q: What is the danger of burning charcoal in a closed room?
options: It gives off a poisonous gas
It makes the room too cold
mcq.explanation: Charcoal fumes can make people ill or worse.

mcq.q: Why should you prepare all the food before lighting the fire?
options: So the fire does not burn while you are still preparing
To cook faster than a cooker
mcq.explanation: Fuel is not wasted waiting.

mcq.q: Which is a benefit of using less fuel?
mcq.explanation: Buying less fuel means spending less.

mcq.q: What is a wild animal?
options: An animal kept in a house
An animal that lives freely in nature
mcq.explanation: Wild animals are not kept by people.

mcq.q: What is used to make the arms of a scarecrow?
options: A shorter stick tied across the pole
mcq.explanation: The cross stick forms shoulders and arms.

mcq.q: Why is poison a bad way to deal with wild animals?
options: It can also kill other animals and people
It is too slow to spread
mcq.explanation: Poison harms living things that are not the target.

mcq.q: What is biodiversity?
options: The variety of living things on Earth
mcq.explanation: Biodiversity includes all the different animals and plants.

mcq.q: Which of these makes a scarecrow shine in the sun?
mcq.explanation: Shiny objects flash and scare animals.

mcq.q: Why does a scarecrow need a hat and clothes?
options: To look like a person and frighten animals
mcq.explanation: Animals fear people, so a figure like a person scares them.

mcq.q: Which crop is established by direct sowing of tiny seeds?
mcq.explanation: Carrots are sown directly because transplanting damages their roots.

mcq.q: How fine should the soil in the seedbed be?
mcq.explanation: Fine crumbly soil lets seeds come up easily.

mcq.q: Why do we mix tiny seeds with dry sand?
options: To spread them thinly and evenly
mcq.explanation: Sand helps prevent clumps of seeds.

mcq.q: When should the grass mulch be removed?
mcq.explanation: Seedlings need light.

mcq.q: How can a person without a garden grow tiny-seeded crops?
options: In a container seedbed with drainage holes
mcq.explanation: A box or tin with holes and fine soil works well.

mcq.q: Which crop can be harvested about four to six weeks after sowing?
mcq.explanation: Radish grows very quickly.

mcq.q: Which of these is a climbing fruit crop?
mcq.explanation: Passion fruit needs support to climb.

mcq.q: What do flowers become in a fruit tree?
mcq.explanation: Fruits develop from flowers.

mcq.q: About how big should a planting hole for a fruit tree be?
options: As big as a football field
About half a metre wide and deep
mcq.explanation: The hole gives roots space in loose soil.

mcq.q: Where should the graft joint of a grafted seedling be?
mcq.explanation: Buried joints can rot or grow roots of the wrong kind.

mcq.q: What is pruning?
options: Cutting off dead, weak or unwanted branches
mcq.explanation: Pruning helps light and air reach the plant.

mcq.q: Why should fruit be washed before eating?
mcq.explanation: Clean fruit is safe to eat.

mcq.q: What is a tree tomato?
options: A woody fruit tree that grows in cooler highlands
mcq.explanation: Tree tomato is a woody tree fruit.

mcq.q: Why do some farmers tie a young tree to a stake?
options: To keep it upright in wind
mcq.explanation: Stakes protect against bending.

mcq.q: Which of these is a benefit of growing your own fruit?
options: Fresh fruit for the family at low cost
mcq.explanation: Growing at home saves money.

mcq.q: Which of these is a sign of a healthy young fruit plant?
mcq.explanation: Healthy plants grow green.

mcq.q: Which group of animals is called poultry?
mcq.explanation: Poultry means birds kept for eggs and meat.

mcq.q: What is a male sheep called?
mcq.explanation: A ram is a male sheep.

mcq.q: Which animal is kept mainly for wool?
mcq.explanation: Some sheep breeds have wool.

mcq.q: Which nutrient in milk builds strong bones and teeth?
mcq.explanation: Milk has calcium and protein.

mcq.q: What is the purpose of vaccinating animals?
mcq.explanation: Vaccination protects animals from diseases.

mcq.q: Which domestic animal is kept as a pet to guard the home?
mcq.explanation: Dogs guard homes.

mcq.q: Which food group gives the body energy?
mcq.explanation: Carbohydrates and fats give energy.

mcq.q: Which of these is a protective food?
mcq.explanation: Vegetables give vitamins and minerals.

mcq.q: Which of these meals is balanced?
mcq.explanation: It includes all three groups.

mcq.q: Which of these gives fibre?
mcq.explanation: Fibre helps digestion.

mcq.q: Which of these can happen if a child eats only ugali?
options: Feeling weak and getting sick often
mcq.explanation: One food cannot supply all nutrients.

mcq.q: Which meal is missing protective foods?
mcq.explanation: Rice and fish have energy and protein but no vegetables or fruits.

mcq.q: What is cooking?
mcq.explanation: Cooking uses heat to make food safe and tasty.

mcq.q: Which food is usually shallow fried?
mcq.explanation: Eggs are commonly fried in a pan.

mcq.q: Who should be with a child who is cooking?
mcq.explanation: An adult helps prevent accidents.

mcq.q: Why should potatoes be cut into pieces of equal size before boiling?
options: They cook at the same time
mcq.explanation: Equal pieces cook evenly.

mcq.q: Why should food be dry before it is put into hot oil?
mcq.explanation: Splashing oil can burn.

mcq.q: Which way should you open a lid on a hot pot?
mcq.explanation: Steam can burn.

mcq.q: Which food may be served with boiled potatoes for a balanced meal?
options: A second helping of potatoes only
mcq.explanation: Vegetables add protective foods.

mcq.q: What is personal hygiene?
options: Keeping our own bodies clean to stay healthy
mcq.explanation: Personal hygiene is care of the body.

mcq.q: What should you use to wash your hands?
mcq.explanation: Soap removes germs.

mcq.q: What should be placed under a tippy tap?
options: A basin or a soak pit
mcq.explanation: To catch the dirty water.

mcq.q: Why should fingernails be kept short?
options: Germs and worm eggs hide under long nails
mcq.explanation: Clean short nails prevent infection.

mcq.q: Why should we wear shoes?
options: To protect feet from injury, worms and jiggers
mcq.explanation: Shoes protect the feet.

mcq.q: Why should you bathe every day?
options: To remove sweat, dirt and germs
mcq.explanation: Bathing keeps the body clean.

mcq.q: Why should combs and towels not be shared?
mcq.explanation: Personal items should be for one person.

mcq.q: Which method uses water and a mop?
mcq.explanation: Mopping washes floors.

mcq.q: In which direction do you sweep a room?
options: From the corners towards the middle or door
mcq.explanation: This gathers dirt in one place.

mcq.q: Which waste should not be burnt because the smoke is harmful?
mcq.explanation: Burning plastics gives harmful smoke.

mcq.q: How can a dustpan be improvised?
options: Cut a jerrican or flat tin
mcq.explanation: A cut jerrican forms a scoop.

mcq.q: Which is recycling?
options: Turning used material into something new
mcq.explanation: Recycling reuses materials.

mcq.q: Why should the compound be free of long grass and rubbish?
options: Snakes, rats and mosquitoes can hide there
mcq.explanation: A tidy compound is safer.

mcq.q: Which PPE protects the head from sun and dust?
mcq.explanation: Hats, caps and scarves cover the head.

mcq.q: What is the first step in cleaning gumboots?
options: Knock off lumps of mud outside
mcq.explanation: This removes the dirt before washing.

mcq.q: Why stuff canvas shoes with paper after washing?
options: It keeps their shape and soaks up moisture
mcq.explanation: Paper absorbs water.

mcq.q: Why should cleaning be done in an open place with drainage?
options: So dirty water does not make a puddle
mcq.explanation: Dirty water can breed mosquitoes.

mcq.q: What should you do if your PPE is damaged?
options: Tell a teacher or an adult
mcq.explanation: Damaged PPE may not protect you.

mcq.q: Which is a correct step for cleaning gloves?
options: Snatch them off by the fingers
Pull them off from the wrist so the dirty outside does not touch skin
mcq.explanation: This prevents germs touching the skin.

mcq.q: In even tacking, the stitches and gaps are
mcq.explanation: Even tacking is equal.

mcq.q: Where should needles be kept?
options: In a pin cushion or needle case
mcq.explanation: Needles are sharp.

mcq.q: Which thread colour is best for tacking?
options: One that shows clearly on the cloth
mcq.explanation: It is easy to see and pull out.

mcq.q: What should you do with tacking when permanent sewing is done?
mcq.explanation: Tacking is temporary.

mcq.q: What size square did we cut for the handkerchief?
mcq.explanation: A small handkerchief is easy to make.

mcq.q: Which is a mistake in tacking?
options: Using small back stitch at the end
Making stitches of different lengths in even tacking
mcq.explanation: Stitches should be equal.

mcq.q: What is a pin cushion used for?
mcq.explanation: It holds sharp objects.

short.q: Name two materials that can be used to make compost.
short.answer: Vegetable peelings, dry leaves, grass, straw or animal dung (any two).

short.q: Explain how to look after a compost heap for two months.
short.answer: Keep it damp like a squeezed sponge, keep it covered, turn it after two to three weeks, and keep children and animals away.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct care activity, up to 4.

short.q: Give two ways in which drip irrigation saves water.
short.answer: It gives water near the roots so little is wasted, and less water evaporates because only a small patch of soil is wet.

short.q: Compare a watering can with drip irrigation.
short.answer: A watering can wets a wide area and much water is lost by running off and by evaporation. Drip irrigation puts water beside the roots slowly, so less is used, fewer weeds grow, and the leaves stay dry.
short.working: 2 marks for the watering can, 2 marks for drip irrigation.

short.q: Give three ways of saving fuel when cooking.
short.answer: Use a lid on the pot, cut food small, use dry firewood, put out the fire after cooking, soak beans first, or use an improved jiko (any three).

short.q: Explain four benefits of conserving fuel.
short.answer: Saves trees and forests, saves money, reduces smoke and illness, saves time looking for firewood.

short.q: Give two reasons why we should not kill wild animals that eat crops.
short.answer: They are part of nature and biodiversity, and they help in other ways such as pollinating and eating pests.

short.q: Give three peaceful ways of protecting crops from birds and animals apart from a scarecrow.
short.answer: Nets, fences, noise makers, shiny objects, guarding at the time animals come (any three).

short.q: Explain what is meant by direct sowing.
short.answer: Sowing seeds straight into the place where the crop will grow until harvest.
short.working: 1 mark for sowing seeds where the crop stays, 1 mark for no transplanting.

short.q: Why should tiny seeds be sown shallowly?
short.answer: They have little stored food so they cannot push up through deep soil.
short.working: 1 mark for little food, 1 mark for not reaching the surface.

short.q: Write the steps for growing carrots from seed to harvest.
short.answer: Prepare a fine seedbed; make drills about 1 cm deep; sow seeds thinly with sand; cover and water gently; thin to about 5 cm; weed and water; harvest after three to four months by loosening the soil and pulling.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct stage, up to 5.

short.q: Describe how to prepare a planting hole for a fruit tree.
short.answer: Choose a sunny site; dig a hole about half a metre wide and deep; put topsoil aside; mix topsoil with compost; put some mixture back in the hole.

short.q: Explain pruning.
short.answer: It is cutting off dead, weak or crossing branches so that light and air can reach the plant.
short.working: 1 mark for cutting, 1 mark for the purpose.

short.q: Explain two mistakes that can spoil a newly planted fruit tree and how to avoid them.
short.answer: Burying the graft joint under the soil, plant with joint above the ground; not watering in dry weather, water regularly.
short.working: 1 mark for each mistake and 1 for each solution.

short.q: Why do some fruit trees take longer to give fruit than others?
short.answer: Big trees such as mango grow slowly and need years before flowering, while pawpaw and passion fruit are small plants that fruit within about a year.
short.working: 1 mark each for slow trees, fast plants, and reason of size or type.

short.q: Give three uses of goats.
short.answer: Meat, milk, skins, manure and income (any three).

short.q: List four basic needs of domestic animals.
short.answer: Clean water, enough feed, clean shelter, health care and kind handling.

short.q: Name the three main food groups and one example of each.
short.answer: Energy-giving: ugali; body-building: beans; protective: sukuma wiki (or other correct examples).
short.working: 1 mark for each group with example.

short.q: Explain why vegetables and fruits should be eaten every day.
short.answer: They give vitamins and minerals, fibre for digestion and water, so they protect the body from disease.

short.q: Prepare a balanced menu for one day for a Grade 4 child using local foods and explain why it is balanced.
short.answer: Breakfast: porridge and egg; lunch: ugali, beans and sukuma wiki; supper: rice, fish and cabbage with fruit. It includes energy, body-building and protective foods in every day.
short.working: 3 marks for a menu with all groups, 2 marks for correct explanation.

short.q: Give two disadvantages of shallow frying.
short.answer: It can splash and burn, and too much oil is not good for health.

short.q: List four safety rules when cooking.
short.answer: Cook with an adult; turn handles inward; use a dry cloth for hot pots; open lids away from the face; keep water away from hot oil (any four).

short.q: What should you do after cooking to keep the kitchen safe and clean?
short.answer: Put out the fire or switch off the gas, wash and store utensils and wipe the working area.
short.working: 1 mark for fire or gas, 1 mark for cleaning.

short.q: State two ways of making drinking water safe.
short.answer: Boil and cool it covered; use a filter or treatment tablets.

short.q: Explain four ways germs can enter the body.
short.answer: Through the mouth from dirty hands, dirty food, dirty water, and through cuts or feet without shoes.

short.q: Explain the meaning of domestic hygiene.
short.answer: Keeping the home and its surroundings clean.
short.working: 1 mark for keeping clean, 1 mark for the home.

short.q: Why should plastic not be burnt?
short.answer: The smoke is harmful to health and the environment.
short.working: 1 mark for harmful smoke, 1 mark for the environment or health.

short.q: Give three reasons why a clean home is important.
short.answer: It prevents diseases, keeps food safe, prevents accidents and looks pleasant.

short.q: Describe how to clean gumboots.
short.answer: Knock off lumps of mud; rinse; scrub with a soft brush and soapy water inside and outside; rinse again; dry upside down in the shade.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four steps.

short.q: State three safety rules when cleaning PPE.
short.answer: Use soap and clean water; keep buckets and brushes from small children; wash your hands after; clean in an open place with drainage.

short.q: Give three uses of tacking stitches.
short.answer: Hold layers of cloth together, mark a line, keep hems in place, help to sew straight (any three).

short.q: Why should a thread colour different from the cloth be used?
short.answer: The stitches are easy to see and to remove.

short.q: Explain how measuring skills help you in tacking.
short.answer: Measuring gives correct stitch lengths, straight lines and correct size of the item.
